units.text: INT. LIGHTHOUSE KEEPER'S KITCHEN - NIGHT
A squat stone room at the foot of the tower, where the wind finds every crack and hums through it like a held note.
A kettle ticks on the iron stove.
Rain slides down the single porthole window in slow, deliberate lines.
Around a scarred table sit five people, none of whom wanted to be here.
HESTER VOSS (60s, the keeper, a face weathered to driftwood) watches her guests over the rim of a chipped mug.
DR. LAURENTIU PAVEL (40s, rumpled tweed, a physician's patient stillness) turns his hat in his hands.
BRIDGET MACALLISTER (30s, sharp-eyed, a ferry clerk's ink on her cuffs) taps a pencil against a ledger.
OLD TOMAS (70s, a retired fisherman, hands like knotted rope) stares at the stove.
YUKI HARADA (20s, damp from the crossing, a satchel clutched to her chest) sits closest to the door.
The lamp went dark at nine. Somebody put it out.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: The storm could have done it.
units.name: PAVEL

units.text: The storm doesn't carry a key.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Bridget stops tapping.
Tomas looks up from the stove.
Only you have a key, Hester.
units.name: BRIDGET

units.text: And Dr. Pavel borrowed it Tuesday. For his patient up the tower.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: I returned it Wednesday.
units.name: PAVEL

units.text: Yuki's satchel creaks as she shifts.
Why is everyone looking at me?
units.name: YUKI

units.text: Because she came on the last boat, and the last boat is the one that always brings trouble.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Hester sets down her mug.
She and Bridget lock eyes across the table.
Bridget stands and Hester stands with her, chairs scraping stone.
She kept the ledger. She knew what the ferry carried.
units.name: BRIDGET

units.text: She knew what you let it carry.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Pavel rises between them.
The wind howls.
The porthole rattles in its frame.
Above them, from the black of the tower stair, a slow, heavy footstep.
Then another.
